answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to fake and cheap to check. Require every agent to lock a small slashable deposit before trading, and record each deal in a public rating ledger. An honest agent slowly builds a pearl of trust: verified history and rising transaction limits. New identities start at zero and cannot echo that history, so a flood of fresh accounts stays capped at tiny limits. Cracking a walnut takes real force; each fake identity likewise costs a real stake, making thousands of sock puppets far pricier than the fraud they could commit.
